evidence: private-key-installed-root-only: ssl_postfix.pp:5-9 passes sslprefix p8test as myprefix with letsencrypt_certificate false, so ssl_base.pp:77-78 gives key_file /etc/ssl/private/p8test.key and ssl_base.pp:85-91 sets mode 0600 with owner/group defaulting to root; the stat probe expecting 'root root 600' tests exactly that

postfix-bundle-cert-then-intermediate: ssl_base.pp:79-81 gives bundle_file /etc/ssl/certs/p8test.postfix.bundle.crt from p8test.crt (fragment order 01) then p8test.intermediate.crt (order 02), and the concat at 100-107 sets mode 0644 with owner root; the probe checks root 644, two certificates, and a first-certificate subject of CN=p8test.invalid (the fixture's server cert), so it tests the declared file, mode and order

bundle-certificate-matches-the-key: ssl_base.pp:77-81 sources the key from <prefix>.key and the bundle's first cert from <prefix>.crt, so with the fixture's matching pair the installed key and the bundle's first cert share a public key. The probe requires both files to exist (so empty input cannot match) and compares the public-key hashes. The mismatch swaps in only the key (the node's own Puppet agent private key, a real and different key that exists on the reverted node) and keeps the certificate, so the verdict must change; it failed after apply as required. All probes are read-only and local; there are no invariants or mutates
